summary: Heroic Patron tier — all 12 backend tests pass and frontend integration verified end-to-end. Wall of Fame heroic-patrons-section renders 2 patron cards with HEROIC PATRON badge, Monthly Sustainer label, charge count 6, ₹3,000 total. No duplication into the regular fame grid. Admin Dashboard Patrons tab present with admin-patrons panel, recompute-patrons-btn (toast: 'Checked 4 subscribers, promoted 2.'), and per-subscription simulate-charge-{id} buttons that fire promotion toasts.
passed_tests: Backend GET /api/heroic-patrons -> 200 list, all entries tier=heroic_patron, sorted desc by patron_charge_count, no _id leakage
Backend POST /api/admin/subscriptions/{id}/simulate-charge requires admin (401/403 without auth)
Backend: 6 simulate-charges on a fresh subscription -> first 5 promoted=False, 6th promoted=True with charge_count=6, plan='monthly', total_amount=3000
Backend GET /api/admin/patrons/summary/{email} returns charge_count>=6, qualified=true, plan=monthly, total_amount>=3000 after 6 charges
Backend: Public /api/heroic-patrons reflects newly promoted user (email lowercased, tier=heroic_patron, patron_charge_count=6, patron_plan=monthly)
Backend POST /api/subscriptions/webhook with subscription.charged + bad signature -> 200 {verified:false, status:received} (no crash, code path safe)
Frontend /wall-of-fame: heroic-patrons-section visible with 2 patron-card-{email} entries; HEROIC PATRON badge, Monthly Sustainer label, 6 contributions, ₹3,000 each
Frontend /wall-of-fame: regular fame grid does NOT duplicate patrons (patrons filtered out via tier!=heroic_patron)
Frontend /dashboard: Patrons tab [data-testid=tab-patrons] activates [data-testid=admin-patrons] panel with [data-testid=recompute-patrons-btn]
Frontend Recompute click -> toast 'Recomputed patrons. Checked 4 subscribers, promoted 2.'
Frontend Simulate-Charge click -> toast '🎉 Promoted to Heroic Patron!' (existing already-qualified sub) and counter updates
critical_code_review_comments: utils/patron.py:get_patron_summary lowercases email but if user signup ever stored mixed-case email this would silently fail to find the user (returns reason='user_not_found' but charge_count is still computed). routes/auth.py register already lowercases on insert, so fine in practice — but worth a unit-level guard or a one-time migration to ensure all db.users emails are lowercased.

routes/subscriptions.py:simulate_charge writes subscription_id = sub.razorpay_subscription_id OR sub.id (fallback). For stub mode the razorpay_subscription_id is 'sub_PENDING_*' which is fine for counting via {$exists:true,$ne:''}. Just note that count_subscription_charges in utils/patron.py only filters by email (not subscription id), so charges across multiple subs of the same email all count toward the 6 threshold — confirm this is the intended product semantics (probably yes; user-level patron tier).
routes/subscriptions.py:webhook persists payload even on bad signature — good for forensics, returns 200 to avoid Razorpay retry storms. Fine.
Frontend Dashboard.js handleSimulateCharge fires fetchData() after each click — a little wasteful when running 6 in a row. Functional, just not optimal. Not a blocker.

patron_card text says 'Heroic Patron with 6 monthly contributions.' — pluralization is fine; for 1 charge (impossible at threshold=6 but for future tunable threshold) it would say '1 monthly contributions'. Cosmetic only.
seed_data_creation: Created 1 test user (test_patron_<uuid>@example.com, role=member) inserted directly via motor (signup requires OTP), and 1 monthly subscription (₹500). Then ran 6 simulate-charge calls -> user is now a Heroic Patron in db.users.badges and db.wall_of_fame. After this run, the public /api/heroic-patrons returns 2 entries (admin@heroichifi.org from previous iteration and the new test patron). DB grew by 1 user + 1 subscription + 6 donations + 1 wall_of_fame entry per run; idempotent across re-runs because uuid emails are unique each time but the assertions don't depend on uniqueness.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Heroic Patron flow is fully wired end-to-end. Tests in /app/backend/tests/test_heroic_patron.py are stable and use a direct-DB seed (motor.AsyncIOMotorClient via config.db) to bypass OTP for the user fixture. Each pytest run inserts a fresh test_patron_<uuid> user + 1 sub + 6 donations + a wall_of_fame entry — DB will accumulate; harmless but cleanup script could prune emails matching ^test_patron_ if storage matters. PATRON_THRESHOLD=6 lives in utils/patron.py. Webhook signature is intentionally invalid in tests because RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET is a placeholder — verified:false path is the one exercised. The Wall of Fame already has admin@heroichifi.org pre-existing as a Heroic Patron from prior manual testing per the review request — that's expected.
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs surfaced. One self-inflicted test bug found and fixed during writing: my test fixture seeded a user with email 'TEST_patron_<uuid>@example.com' (capitalised) but utils/patron.py:promote_if_qualified lowercases the lookup, so the user wasn't found. Fixed by lowercasing the seed email — matches what /api/auth/register does in production code. Lesson: any direct-DB seed must mirror the lower().strip() normalisation that the auth route applies.
